issues.failure_explanation: The solution operator \(\mathcal{A}\) has eigenvalue \(\mu=1/(\beta-\lambda)\). Its second component \(T\) therefore satisfies \(T u = \mu u\), so the eigenpair of \(T\) is \((\mu,u)\), not \((\lambda,u)\). The definitions of \(R(\lambda_j)\), \(R_h(\lambda_j)\), and the adjoint analogues are consequently based on the wrong parameter, making the \(L^2\)-gap estimate (a3.22) in Theorem th3.1 ill-posed as stated.

issues.failure_explanation: The two displayed coefficients are positive only if \(\varepsilon_4 > c^*/(\gamma c_*)\) and \(\varepsilon_4 < c_*/c^*\). Such an \(\varepsilon_4\) exists only when \(c^*/(\gamma c_*) < c_*/c^*\), i.e. \((c^*/c_*)^2 < \gamma\). Since \(c^*\ge c_*\), this condition is not guaranteed for all \(\gamma>1\) or for arbitrary stabilization parameters. The proof therefore does not establish Lemma 3.1 in general.

To obtain the stated rate \(h^{2\min(l,s)}\), the proof implicitly uses the same \(H^{1+s}\) regularity for the adjoint eigenfunctions. The theorem only assumes \(M(\lambda_j)\subset H^{1+s}\times H^{1+s}\); no analogous hypothesis is stated for \(M^*(\lambda_j^*)\). Without it, the bound on the adjoint error term is unsupported.
